plan: Given my private value of $20, I should bid slightly below my value to maximize profit while ensuring a win. Bidding exactly my value or higher risks no profit. Rational bidders will bid below their own values, anticipating the same from others. Thus, I will bid slightly below $20 to outbid others likely bidding below their values. This strategy balances winning the auction and maximizing profit.

Given my private value of $24, I should bid slightly below my value to maximize profit while still having a high chance of winning. Considering rational opponents, they will bid up to their values. To avoid overpaying, I will bid $0.1 below my value. This strategy balances winning probability and profit maximization, as the second-highest bid will likely be just below my bid, minimizing costs if I win.

As a rational bidder, I'll bid slightly above the expected average of other bids to maximize profit. With values uniformly distributed between $0 and $20, the average is $10. To outbid others while ensuring profit, I'll bid slightly above this average but below my value. A bid of $15 should outbid others without risking overpayment.
